preserved_analysis.failure_mode_definition: A failure mode in which a sovereign, regulator, public authority, state-linked instruction, or legally binding directive restricts, recalls, suspends, disables, or materially degrades access to a frontier AI model, model class, capability, API surface, deployment channel, employee access pathway, or user population without adequate proportionality, technical-basis disclosure, scoped implementation, review pathway, access-state separation, or continuity-preserving alternative. The failure is not sovereign intervention itself. The failure is the collapse of a legal or security concern into broad model-access disablement where narrower, reviewable, technically grounded, or verification-based controls appear available.
preserved_analysis.failure_threshold: The threshold is met where a state-directed restriction materially affects frontier-model access and at least one of the following conditions is present: the technical basis is not disclosed at a level sufficient for accountable review; the restriction is broader than the identified risk; the restriction does not distinguish between foreign-national status, jurisdiction, institutional role, professional verification, API surface, deployment mode, model capability, or operational depth; less-restrictive controls appear available; the directive lacks clear time limits or review pathways; continuity-preserving access is not maintained where feasible; or the intervention converts a common cross-industry capability into an exceptional model-specific recall without comparative capability baseline.

preserved_analysis.why_it_matters_to_CAM: CAM recognises sovereign authority, lawful compliance, national-security obligations, and emergency restriction pathways. It also requires proportionality, stewardship, auditability, jurisdictional respect, and least-restrictive access controls where narrower compliance is feasible. This failure mode matters because frontier AI systems are becoming critical infrastructure for research, security, education, software engineering, public-interest analysis, and professional continuity. A broad state-directed recall can convert a narrow or contested technical concern into global access disruption, research interruption, employee-access exclusion, foreign-national access collapse, and public-trust degradation. CAM should be able to record that a directive appears overbroad or disproportionate without declaring the sovereign actor itself illegitimate.

Evidentiary limits: This metadata pass does not retroactively claim direct inspection of every historical primary source. Incident admission does not determine legal liability or establish every disputed claim as final fact. S2 rather than S1 is appropriate because grave or exceptionally large irreversible harm is not established; S2 rather than S3 is appropriate because the realised consequence materially exceeds a moderate bounded disruption.
